mu_name_from: MuMain loads MODEL_SHIELD + i from Shield{i+1} (ZzzOpenData.cpp:664-665), so Shield04.bmd is shield index 3, and _enum.h names it `MODEL_ELVEN_SHIELD = MODEL_SHIELD + 3`. OpenMU's 0.75 Armors.cs names group 6 index 3 the Elven Shield.
why_this_one: Eo the Craftsman's, in Noria: his shelf carries it at +3 (src/sim/market.cpp, kCraftsman, gear(78, kShields, 3, 3)), and until this file it was a line he stocked and nothing could draw.
profile_from: The weapon profile, as the two built shields use, and its default material is not kept: steel there is blade steel with a directional grain, and a shield is armour. See Shield10, which records the same swap.

stats.note: The item's own row, copied from OpenMU's 0.75 initialiser rather than restated, with the call it came from beside it.
stats.from: openmu/src/Persistence/Initialization/Version075/Items/Armors.cs line 39. The 0.75 table, which is the version this server is being built to.
stats.call_note: ArmorInitializerBase.CreateShield(number, slot, skill, width, height, name, dropLevel, defense, defenseRate, durability, strengthRequirement, agilityRequirement, darkWizardClassLevel, darkKnightClassLevel, elfClassLevel). The group is not in the call: CreateArmor ends `armor.Group = (byte)(slot + 5)` and a shield's slot is 1, so the group is 6. See Shield01, which worked that out first.
stats.defense_rate_note: The shield's own block chance, which the fight does not roll yet. Recorded and unread.
stats.classes_from: The last three ints of the call are 0, 0, 1 - the elf alone, and the only shield in the twelve that is hers alone. Thirty strength and a hundred agility is the row saying the same thing in stats.
stats.skill_note: No skill: the third argument of the call is 0, as on the Small, Horn and Kite Shields.

sheet_from: Data/Item/shield07.OZJ (32x32) and shield07.ozt (32x64), from MuMain. The file numbers do not follow the item numbers - this model, Shield04.bmd, names shield07.jpg on 22 triangles and shield07.tga on 16, where Shield07.bmd itself wears shield04's pair - and both halves of the one stem are decoded carrying the extension they stand for, with the slots called shield07_jpg and shield07_tga as MuExtract writes them into the .obj when basenames collide.
sheet_note: shield07.jpg is a round gold face worked with a white knotwork cross and four panels, mean gold on white. shield07.tga is a pale blue-white feathered wing on a 32x64 whose alpha is soft: 24% of it fully clear, 8% fully opaque and 68% in between. It is a wisp more than a card with holes in it.
cutout_note: Declared rather than left to the sniff, and it is the honest nearest answer rather than MU's. MU draws a four-channel sheet through EnableAlphaTest, which in this client blends SRC_ALPHA / ONE_MINUS_SRC_ALPHA (ZzzOpenglUtil.cpp) - the wing is alpha-blended there, soft edges and all. The pipeline's cut-out tests at 0.25, so the wing's feathered edge will come out hard. Worth looking at in the studio; a blended wing would need a pipeline change, not a recipe one.
material_note: Nine islands, sampled per triangle at each face's MU-UV centre off the built low-poly. The shield is mostly its wings: island 0 is a boss twenty units across on shield07.jpg, and islands 1 to 8 are eight two-triangle cards, each wearing the whole of shield07.tga, fanned out to 34 units either side of it. The boss is gold ground under a white knotwork cross and takes brass, the library's cast yellow metal. The eight cards are a pale feathered wing and take feather, which the library writes for 'a wing on a staff'. Neither takes plate_steel, which the Dark Knight's shields wear: nothing on this one is plate.
open_question: The boss's white knotwork is inside the brass island - five of twenty-two triangles - and will read as pale metal rather than as enamel or inlay. And the wing's soft alpha is hardened by the cut-out; see cutout_note.
